item.title: Happy Camper for Saturday, January 31, 2026
item.description: Has it been 30 years since we started counting whales and other “ocean critters” (that’s the term of Jean Souza, the Hawaiian Islands Humpback Whale National Sanctuary Kauai person, and the on-site manager for the Ocean Discovery center at Kukui Grove Center)?

item.title: EDITORIAL: ICE violence spurs legislative action
item.description: Wherever one falls on the political spectrum, the shooting death of U.S. citizen and ICU nurse Alex Pretti by a swarm of immigration enforcement agents at a Minneapolis protest is a national tragedy. Pretti’s death symbolizes all that has gone terribly wrong with the Immigration and Customs Enforcement surge that originally, maybe even palatably, was billed as a purge of the “worst of the worst” from U.S. soil.

item.title: Red Raiders ladies advance to Div. II state semis
item.description: HONOLULU — Kauai High School soccer, seeded No. 3 at the 2026 Hele Hawaii High School Athletic Association Girls Soccer State Championships Division II bracket, advanced to the semifinals following a 2-1 edge over the Hawaii Preparatory Academy on Thursday at the Waipio Peninsula Soccer Complex on Oahu.

item.title: Teachers, parents divided over proposed Hawaii school cellphone ban
item.description: Cellphones and all other telecommunication devices would be banned in Hawaii’s public schools under a House bill that attempts to resolve a divisive issue, even among Hawaii’s public school teachers.

item.title: Police seek public’s help to locate missing man
item.description: LIHUE — The Kauai Police Department (KPD) is requesting the public’s assistance in locating a man who was reported missing.

item.title: Math at center of Hawaii’s education priorities for 2026 session
item.description: Math readiness has emerged as a defining education issue for Hawaii as lawmakers and school leaders prepare for the 2026 legislative cycle, framing numeracy not only as an academic concern but as a foundation for workforce readiness, economic mobility and long-term student success.

item.title: Distressed hikers rescued on Kalalau Trail Thursday
item.description: LIHUE — Personnel from the Kauai Fire Department rescued a 51-year-old male German visitor from the Kalalau Trail on Thursday, along with one minor hiking with him.

item.title: Staying visible: A peaceful rally honoring victims of Minnesota shootings
item.description: Kauai Indivisible hosted a peaceful “visibility” rally that attracted about 200 people on Thursday to the sidewalks fronting Kaumualii Highway near the Kauai Community College.
